notes: ROBOTS: https://www.westwing.co.uk/robots.txt fetched FIRST. It DOES name ClaudeBot, Claude-Web and anthropic-ai, but they sit in one combined AI-crawler group shared with GPTBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot etc., and that group is NOT a 'Disallow: /' opt-out. Its directives are byte-identical to the generic 'User-agent: *' block plus one extra 'Allow: /llms.txt': Allow /new-products/$, /customer/invitation/create/, */customer/invitation/create/; Disallow /all-products, /p/s/*, /customer*, *--*, /*?*q=*, *?c=, *&c=, /sso/*, /c/*, /products/*, /collections/*, /api/*. It is therefore not more restrictive for Claude than for any other agent, and none of those prefixes matches this site's category-listing pattern, which is a flat slug off the root (/toilet-brushes/, /bathroom-storage/). Every URL below was checked against that list: no query string, no double hyphen, no /c/, /products/, /collections/ or /api/ prefix. I did NOT touch /api/* at any point - all quantities come from rendered HTML. No Crawl-delay declared; probe.py's 2 s per-host gap was honoured. Same reading as the validated SR 91 Westwing UK Furniture pass and the Westwing IT pass. ACCESS: plain direct fetch via probe.py (curl_cffi firefox133 / chrome) throughout - no proxy, no impersonation tricks, no jina, no translate.goog, no 403s. TREE SOURCE: the real mega-menu, not guessed URL patterns. The storefront is a Shopify Oxygen/Hydrogen React-Router app whose full navigation is embedded in the homepage as a flattened turbo-stream payload (window.__reactRouterContext.streamController.enqueue). I concatenated the 7 enqueue chunks, JSON-unescaped them and raw-decoded the 5,481-entry reference array, then resolved the node graph (key _67 = label, _276 = path, _541 = children) back into the complete 503-node, 3-level menu across all 14 top-level departments (work/w89_92/ww_nav.txt). Cross-checked against /sitemap-categories.xml (563 category URLs) to catch live collections that exist but are not linked from the nav - that surfaced Shower curtains (7) and Bathrobes (3), both routed to Textile and both logged in review. TREE SHAPE: Westwing has NO top-level Bathroom department. Bathroom content is distributed across 'Home accessories > Bathroom accessories' (9 children - the real accessories tree), 'Textiles > Bathroom textiles' (3 children), 'Furniture > Wardrobes > Bathroom cabinets', 'Furniture > Shelves > Bathroom shelves', 'Storage > Small storage & organisers > Bathroom accessories', 'Rugs > By room > Bathroom' and a 'Shop by room > Bathroom' hub. Westwing is a decor retailer: a keyword sweep of all 563 sitemap category URLs and all 503 nav nodes for tap|faucet|shower|toilet|basin|sink|sanitary|bidet|bathtub returned only toilet roll holders, toilet brushes, shower curtains and kitchen sink organisers - there are genuinely no baths, toilets, basins, taps, showers or enclosures (rules 4-8 have no nodes here). QTY METHOD: rendered listing header only - no API was used (robots disallows /api/*). Every leaf's count was taken from the page's own sort/filter bar ('50 products') and independently confirmed by the page's own 'X of N products' pagination line. VERIFICATION: three independent figures were required to agree on every recorded leaf, and did, 8 of 8 - filter-bar count, 'N of N products' line, and a direct count of rendered product tiles (div.product-cell-price-wrapper) in the same HTML: Soap dispensers 71/71/71, Toothbrush holders 27/27/27, Bathroom storage 59/59/59, Bathroom bins 49/49/49, Toilet brushes 50/50/50, Toilet roll holders 30/30/30, Towel racks 32/32/32, Makeup mirrors 13/13/13. Each page's <h1> was also read and matched the requested node (e.g. 'Toilet roll holders', 'Makeup mirrors'). All 8 leaves are under Westwing's 120-per-page limit so the tile count is a full enumeration, not a first page. Counts discriminate (3, 7, 12, 13, 27, 29, 30, 32, 37, 43, 49, 50, 51, 59, 71, 111, 205, 312, 414). DEDUP: dedup.already_extracted() run on all 40 candidate URLs. 2 hits, both Furniture.xlsx SR 91 Westwing UK - Bathroom Cabinets (/bathroom-cabinets/, 29) and Bathroom Shelves (/bathroom-shelves/, 37). Both in `review`, neither in `rows`. DUPLICATE-SLUG HANDLING: Westwing re-slugs the same collection under each nav parent (-2, -3 suffixes). I fetched every variant and compared counts: 9 of 11 are exactly count-identical to their canonical URL (e.g. /bathroom-bins-2/ 49 = /bathroom-bins/ 49, /towels-2/ 205 = /towels/ 205), so each product type is recorded once at its canonical slug per rule 28. The 2 that differ (/bathroom-cabinets-2/ 53 vs 29, /bathroom-accessories-2/ 171 vs 312) are documented individually in `review`.
